# BAD-017 — Storage manager that shows each scene version's reclaimable size and deletes versions and takes

## Brief
From BadTakes TODO.md item 39 (added 2026-08-18). The scene library layout's phases 1 and 2 shipped, so the blocker is gone. Versioning keeps every edit forever: a scene reworked ten times holds ten snapshots plus every take recorded against each, and nothing in the app shows that or offers a way to reclaim the space except the Finder.

Shape: a per-scene tree with two branches, an aggregate takes node (every take across every version, so recordings can be cleared without touching the payload) and one node per version (its payload plus the takes recorded against it). Each node has a delete control that removes it and everything beneath.

The trap: sizes must be exclusive, not apparent. Versions hardlink unchanged media from their parent, so a 28 MB video shared by five versions occupies 28 MB once. Each node shows what deleting it would actually free (bytes whose only remaining links are under that node), du-style, one inode counted once. Consequences: a node's exclusive size changes as siblings are deleted; the branches overlap by construction (a version's takes appear under both the version and the aggregate), so the numbers do not sum to the scene total and the UI must not imply they do.

Rules to decide: deleting a version deletes its takes; deleting the head version either refuses or moves head to the newest survivor; deleting a version another scene was forked from must not break the fork (its own hardlinks keep the bytes, which exclusive accounting already reflects).

Read src/CLAUDE.md on the versioned library first. Verify with unit tests over a fixture tree with hardlinks, plus SMOKE_SCOPE=home for the UI.
